To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
using multiple processes and kernel level threads on a SMP cluster can improve the performance of DSM programs significantly.

(1) multiple processes on multiple SMP nodes are a good solution for some programs, (2) multiple threads on multiple SMP nodes can improve the performance for some programs, and (3) kernel threads are a good solution that can improve the performance of most programs on multiple SMP nodes.
a multi-threaded DSM system can provide good performance, and the performance is further enhanced if multiple application threads can be used on each SMP node.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a DSM system that is able to exploit multiple processors on the nodes in a cluster, and the results indicate that this can be done successfully.
the design of high performance distributed shared memories for clusters of SMPs.
how to design a DSM system that can take advantage of the multi-threaded capabilities of the underlying operating system, in order to provide high-performance on a cluster of SMPs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of multiple threads on SMP nodes can be beneficial, but only when the application is written to exploit the parallelism in the program.
Strings is a high performance DSM system for clusters of SMPs, but the performance of the system is dependent on the application and the number of nodes used in the cluster.
the use of kernel level threads is the key to achieving high performance on such systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a multi-threaded runtime environment for DSM systems is a promising direction, but there are several open issues to be resolved.
the performance of Strings can be significantly improved by using a multi-threaded runtime and kernel threads on SMP nodes.
the performance of Strings is comparable to the performance of a message passing library on a cluster of SMPs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
using multiple threads on SMP nodes is a viable alternative to using message passing libraries, and can provide significant performance improvement for some applications.
a multi-threaded runtime environment is essential for high performance on clusters of SMPs.
the design decisions in a high performance DSM can have a significant impact on the performance of a program.
